outlook.statement: The outlook for the Company's business remains positive, supported by the continued growth of India's logistics and transportation sector. Government initiatives relating to infrastructure development, dedicated freight corridors, road and rail connectivity, logistics parks and digitalisation are expected to improve the efficiency of the logistics ecosystem.

The Company intends to leverage the increasing demand for transportation and logistics services arising from industrial growth, e-commerce, retail and the expansion of direct-to-consumer businesses. The Company also sees opportunities to strengthen its service offerings by providing value-added logistics services and adopting technology-enabled solutions for better operational efficiency and customer service.

The Company expects to focus on sustainable growth by expanding its customer base, strengthening relationships with transport contractors and industrial customers, and increasing the utilisation of its existing logistics capabilities.

risks: Increasing Competition: New-age technology logistics startups are entering the market and introducing competing products and services.

Technology Adoption: The logistics industry is required to quickly adopt the latest technologies, including GPS/GIS tracking of consignments, in order to improve efficiency and meet the changing requirements of customers.
Need for Value-Added Services: Logistics companies are expected to expand their product basket to include value-added services such as packaging, labelling and reverse logistics.

Changing Customer Requirements: The need for logistics companies to cater to corporates seeking to outsource their logistics requirements and to provide services in line with evolving customer expectations.
Competitive Pressure on Yields: The logistics industry has witnessed intensifying competitive trends, with yields also being challenged.

Economic and Industry Conditions: The Company's operations may be influenced by domestic and global demand and supply conditions, sales volumes and selling prices, input availability and cost, tax laws, economic developments, litigation and industrial relations.

Dependence on Government Initiatives and Infrastructure: The development of the logistics sector is linked with government initiatives relating to infrastructure, connectivity, logistics parks, warehousing and digitalisation.
Fluctuations in economic conditions, demand and supply, transportation costs and other operating expenses may impact profitability.
Rapid technological developments may require continuous investment and adaptation.
Changes in government policies, taxation, regulatory requirements and infrastructure conditions may affect the Company's operations.
Increasing competition and pressure on yields within the logistics industry may impact margins and customer retention.
